lede: (one chain, five complexions. the headline is the hex colour sampled from her collarbone in the picture; the strip beneath shows all five, and the chain is the constant.)
idea: Every for-every-skin-tone campaign names the tones, and in India the names are the problem. This set names no one. It samples the colour of each woman's collarbone from the image, prints the number as the headline, and lines all five up under the same chain. The Toggle Link Chain is the deepest stock in the catalogue at 80 units, so the set can run for months without a swap.
type: The hex code in Velista at 150px with the hash in Jost and oxblood, a full stop after it because it is a sentence. One line of Cormorant italic beneath. Then the five-cell strip: a square crop of each toggle, a bar of the sampled colour, the code in JetBrains Mono, the current card outlined in a hairline with its code in oxblood. The foot carries the name, the listing's spec, the price and the CTA on one line.
review: Pass 1: the price collided with the strip on every story frame and on the one feed card whose aside ran to two lines; the top-right label vanished on the two cards with dark hair in that corner. Pass 2: plates shortened, the price moved onto the CTA line, every aside cut to one line, the two dark-hair cards given an ivory label with an ink logo, the story spec shortened so it holds one line.
verdict: the strip is the ad; any one card sells the chain, all five together sell the brand.
